punchline: When colleagues refused to fund his four-drug idea for childhood leukemia, Freireich ran it as a separate trial.
thirty_sec: Emil Freireich joined the National Cancer Institute in 1955 to care for children with leukemia. Around 1962 he proposed combining four drugs; colleagues were wary and funding was refused at first, so the trial ran separately. Combination chemotherapy followed, and he shared the 1972 Lasker Award.
question: Which idea your colleagues keep rejecting could you turn into a small separate test with an agreed measure?
key_contrast: Do not win the argument, make the test cheap.
